editorial:
War of the Worlds (2025) puts you in the shoes of Will Radford, a Homeland Security analyst who spends his days watching threats through a huge surveillance system. When a strange attack hits, his usual confidence cracks, and he starts digging into whether the government is hiding the truth. The movie moves like a tense thriller, mixing big sci-fi ideas with personal doubt, so you feel both the danger outside and the pressure inside. It has enough action to keep you alert, but the real hook is watching Will realize the system he trusts may not be telling him everything.

The acting keeps the story grounded, especially when the pressure rises and Will has to choose between following orders and protecting people. The pacing is mostly strong, though some middle scenes slow down while setting up the mystery. The effects look sharp, and the sound design makes the attacks feel loud and close. If you enjoy government conspiracy stories with alien danger, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Will learns the government knew about the unknown entity and used the attack to expand its surveillance powers. He steals the hidden files and broadcasts them to the public, exposing the cover-up. The twist is that the entity was reacting to a government signal, not invading on its own. Once Will shuts down the signal, the attacks stop, and the movie ends with him choosing to protect ordinary people instead of the system.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves government conspiracy thrillers with alien action.
